articles.title: Anantnag becomes India's first district to complete 1.57 lakh Digital Holistic Progress Cards
articles.content: Top Stories Anantnag becomes India’s first district to complete 1.57 lakh Digital Holistic Progress Cards Achieves 100% coverage across 1,444 govt, private schools; sets benchmark for competency-based learning, holistic assessment Arif Rashid 22 Nov 2026 03:52 IST Follow Us Srinagar, Nov 21: In a major milestone for the education sector, Anantnag district of Kashmir Division has become the first district in the country to complete 157,860 Digital Holistic Progress Cards (HPCs), covering 1,444 government and private schools, including CBSE-affiliated institutions. The achievement marks a significant step towards transforming the assessment system from conventional examination-based evaluation to a more comprehensive, competency-based approach that focuses on the overall development of students. An official of the School Education Department said the initiative was launched in May 2025, when the district began providing on-site academic support to teachers at cluster and school levels through faculty members of the District Institute of Education and Training (DIET) Anantnag. The programme focused on Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN), PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan, competency-based learning and the implementation of Holistic Progress Cards. "For nearly two years, our DIET resource teams conducted walkthroughs of the demo Holistic Progress Card available on the PARAKH portal. Thousands of teachers became familiar with its philosophy and framework during 2025 and 2026, even before the Ministry of Education introduced its digital version in August-September 2026," the official said. Recognising HPC as a transformative initiative in competency-based learning and assessment, the PARAKH Team Anantnag, under the leadership of the Chief Education Officer, Principal DIET and District Education Planning Officer (DEPO), devised a phased implementation strategy. The process began with PM SHRI Schools, followed by all government schools and subsequently private educational institutions. Initially, Heads of Institutions, teachers of PM SHRI Schools, School Nodal Officers (SNOs) and teachers from government and private institutions were oriented through online sessions about the philosophy of holistic assessment and its digital framework. However, realising that HPC implementation was much more than a routine data-entry exercise and required a fundamental understanding of pedagogical transformation, the district subsequently organised face-to-face training sessions, supported by continuous online and offline guidance. Zonal Master Trainers played a crucial role by extending on-call and on-site academic and technical assistance to teachers to ensure that the actual objectives of the initiative were understood and implemented effectively. "From school logins, teacher and student registrations, Parts A, B and C, summative marks, NCrF credit scores, APAAR logins, DigiLocker and the Academic Bank of Credits portal to the final generation and completion of HPCs, the journey has been extraordinary," the official said. He added that achieving 100 per cent completion in government schools in October and subsequently bringing every private school on board was a remarkable accomplishment. The official acknowledged that the actual spirit of the Holistic Progress Card lies in continuous assessment throughout the academic session rather than completing the exercise within a limited timeframe.
